name: e with line below = open e, as in "let, there"
source: Christaller 1879, key to the letters (scan seq. 8): vowel class I

name: capital open E
source: Christaller 1879, key to the letters (scan seq. 8)

name: o with line below = open o, as in "not, nor"
source: Christaller 1879, key to the letters (scan seq. 8): vowel class I

name: capital open O
source: Christaller 1879, key to the letters (scan seq. 8)

name: dot under e, o, a: ẹ ọ = class I e/o "diminished, approaching i, u"; ạ = "thin" a (class II)
source: Christaller 1879, key to the letters (scan seq. 8): "I. a e̲ o̲, ẹ ọ; II. ạ e o, i u"

name: macron = long vowel
source: Christaller 1879, key (scan seq. 8): "a ā ... short and long"; seen p. 4 (proverbs 73-74)

name: tilde = nasal vowel
source: Christaller 1879, key (scan seq. 8): "ã ẽ ĩ õ ũ are nasal"

name: breve = very short vowel
source: Christaller 1879, key (scan seq. 8): "ă ĕ ĭ ŏ ŭ are very short"

name: acute = high or middle tone; on syllabic m, n, ṅ printed as a mark after the letter (m′, typed ’)
source: Christaller 1879, key (scan seq. 8): "á é ... m' n' ṅ' have high or middle tone"

name: grave = low tone
source: Christaller 1879, key (scan seq. 8): "à è ... low tone"; seen p. 4 (proverbs 70-71)

name: mark over w: w̌ = "wy" (rounded and palatal); also in tw̌, dw̌, fw̌. Type shape (caron or breve) to verify
source: Christaller 1879, key (scan seq. 8): "w̌ = wy"; encoding as U+030C is a choice, see ORTHOGRAPHY.md

name: ṅ = ng as in "sing" (velar nasal). A dot also appears over s in mmuṡũa: meaning unknown
source: Christaller 1879, key (scan seq. 8): "ṅ = ng in sing"; the s-dot is open question O2

name: circumflex: not in the key; seen on â in nâ, mmâã, ṅkonyâã (meaning unknown)
